subject: Research request: FBI file 105-9673 ("Kohler, Walter"), RG 65, Box 156
body:
Dear NARA reference staff,

One person directs this project and sends this message; the archival research and the audits are done by AI agents (Claude models) working in an open repository, every step logged. We study Walter Koehler, a German agent who transmitted five radio messages to Abwehr stations in France in February 1944 while working as an FBI double agent; the messages themselves were printed enciphered by David Kahn in Cryptologia 5(2) (1981); we have not been able to read them. We have not found any published account of how they were enciphered.

We located, in NARA's own released FBI name-index material (the 2004 Nazi War Crimes Disclosure Act list), an entry for an FBI headquarters file on "Kohler, Walter": RG 65, Class 105, File 9673, Section 001 (and a second section, "EBF 003"), Box 156, location 230 86/16/05. We have not been able to find an item-level online catalogue record for this file, and do not know its contents.

We would be grateful for two things: (1) whether staff can tell from the file description or a quick look whether it discusses Koehler's February 1944 Paris radio traffic or how it was enciphered, and (2) what it would cost to have relevant pages copied if it does. We understand this may need a formal reference request or FOIA process, and are happy to follow whatever is the right route.

What we have on this target, including the search log, is open at https://github.com/NoAutopilot/cipher-lab/tree/main/ciphers/koehler-1944 .

[SIGN-OFF]
notes: Draft file did not exist before this job; written from ASKS row 55 and ciphers/koehler-1944/ARCHIVE.md. Address archives2reference@nara.gov verified today (26 Sept 2026) on archives.gov/dc-metro/college-park's Textual Consultation section; the general archives.gov/contact page gives only inquire@nara.gov, which is less specific. koehler-1944 is a NEAR.md row (open per check-solved) -- this request does not touch that status, it is a pure archival lookup.
